chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Sulayman ibn Ja'far who said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a virgin woman who performed Hajj on behalf of a virgin woman. He said: It is not proper.

key_terms.الرُّضَا: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim or Imam Ali al-Rida depending on context, here used as a title for the Imam.
key_terms.صَرُورَةٍ: A virgin (female), referring to a woman who has not been married.
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: It is not proper / not fitting / not valid.

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj on behalf of another woman according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the juristic nuance of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* or representation by noting that a virgin woman performing Hajj for another virgin woman is 'not proper' (la yanbaghi). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical capability and specific conditions of the representative, distinguishing between mere validity and the preferred or optimal form of worship based on the gender and status of the pilgrim.
